name: Specification selection pass rate
purpose: Measures whether a request is answered with the records it concerns (and with nothing when no record concerns it) without returning a crowd, over the real index of the ESOI repository's records, with a real cheap-model judge and a real local vector search.
record: Cases passed out of cases run for each implementation on the same labelled requests (every expected id present, no more than a ceiling returned), per kind, one row per run in the results log pinned to the commit and the case hash. Every model call is a real one, so a run costs real tokens and the pass rate moves a little between runs. The scripted-judge plumbing checks (batching, invented ids, failed calls) are unit tests, not this metric. The leaderboard ranks the arms by a balanced score of accuracy, cost and time, weighted in esoi.toml [balance.spec_selection].
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=competitive | when=the lexical_vector offline arm of spec_selection runs the whole case set with no model call, validating the cases and scorer before any model is paid for] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a single real case runs end to end and is hand-read] > live [real=yes | max-age-days=90 | when=a person approved the spend under the metric run policy]
command: esoi run spec_selection --impl lexical_vector_gated; esoi run spec_selection --impl lexical_vector_llm; esoi run spec_selection --impl lexical_vector; esoi run spec_selection --impl lexical_only

name: Milestone next-step readiness
purpose: Measures how ready a milestone's next step is, as the first stage of the milestone's own metric when that value cannot move in one turn because it needs people. The step is ready when it has an owner the milestone's record lists, a due date this week, the solution link and the metric link, a concrete kept deliverable with no slot left to fill, and the step only a person can do named. Each increment of the AI should move this stage even when the milestone's own value stays where it is.
record: Items held out of five, read from the milestone's keyed goal by code with no model (milestone_readiness.measure), reported as `<n> of <total>` with what each item is, from the goal before the write and from the goal as the write read it back, beside the milestone metric before and after (an unchanged value is said as unchanged, with why). One reading per milestone turn; the cases are the milestone cases of the private QAR dataset, which are scored by the evaluation of record, not copied here.
disadvantages: Counts presence, not quality: a kept deliverable can be complete and still weak, which the quality stage of the evaluation of record judges. The five items weigh the same.
cascading_conditionals: offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=milestone_readiness.measure counts the items of a goal from records only, with no model call, over synthetic goals in tests/test_milestone_readiness.py] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a single real milestone case runs end to end by decision and the readiness before and after is hand-read against the goal]
